title: Subtract template decoration before adding style
summary: Remove stacked default decorations until one accent, one voice and a type hierarchy remain, then rebuild that decision in the user stack.
when_to_use: An existing interface looks like an untouched generator template.
avoid_when: The user has already specified a deliberate, documented visual system.

anatomy.purpose: Names the one job of the screen before any new decoration.
Keeps a single accent color for primary action, not for every card.
Creates order with size and space rather than extra fonts and colored words.
Deletes decorations that do not serve the decision.

tokens.name: color.accent
tokens.purpose: The only decorative color, used for the primary action.

tokens.name: space.section
tokens.purpose: The gap that separates sections when color is not doing that job.

states.name: review
states.behavior: Lists decorations that were removed and the decision they failed to serve.

responsive: Re-check hierarchy at narrow widths after decorations are removed, because spacing, not color, has to carry it.
accessibility: After reducing color, confirm text and controls still meet contrast.
Do not leave status meaning encoded only in a colored dot or border.
implementation_steps: State what the screen must help the user do.
Remove decorations that do not serve that decision.
Map the remaining accent and spacing onto the project tokens.
Rewrite the affected views in the current stack instead of pasting a sample stylesheet.
